credits.title: Juste la fin du monde
credits.overview: A staging of Jean-Luc Lagarce's play "It's Only the End of the World" by François Berreur.

credits.overview: "At the end of the war, despite the loss of one of their two daughters at Auschwitz and with the vain hope of finding the other entrusted to the Carmelites, a dentist and his wife are trying at all costs to return to life. Perhaps the Promised Land will heal their sorrows ... "

credits.title: Sommeil blanc
credits.overview: A young woman painter living in a chalet away from the world one morning crosses the path of a young boy who will gradually invade his daily life. The young woman will seek to unravel her mystery.

credits.title: The Red Violin
credits.overview: 300 years of a remarkable musical instrument. Crafted by the Italian master Bussotti (Cecchi) in 1681, the red violin has traveled through Austria, England, China, and Canada, leaving both beauty and tragedy in its wake. In Montreal, Samuel L Jackson plays an appraiser going over its complex history.

credits.title: Mange ta soupe
credits.overview: A young man returns to the family home to face a childhood trauma: his brother's suicide, but nobody in the family is willing to help him.

credits.title: A Self-Made Hero
credits.overview: Set in France at the end of World War II Albert Dehousse finds out his father wasn't a war hero and his mother is a collaborator.

credits.title: The Crisis
credits.overview: Victor is a legal advisor who finds himself abandoned by his wife and fired the same day. He tries to seek comfort from different friends and family members, but everyone he meets is concerned with their own problems. His morale begins to falter when he realizes that no one cares about him.
